My name is not important, but I am a mother farming here in Iringa on our small piece of land. This maize plot is only a small part of what we have, and I intercrop it with beans like my mother taught me, so the soil stays strong. I cannot afford much chemical fertilizer — maybe a small bag of urea if the price is fair at the agrodealer in town — but I will put manure from our goats because that costs me nothing but my back. I will use the seed I saved from last year, because the hybrid seed at the shop is too expensive for such a small plot, and I pray the rains come on time so I do not need to pay anyone to help me weed.
